question: Severe acute pancreatitis with confirmed pancreatic necrosis on CT is best managed by immediate surgical debridement (necrosectomy) performed within the first 72 hours of onset.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is FALSE. Early necrosectomy carries very high mortality in acute pancreatitis. The mainstay is supportive care; intervention is delayed until necrosis becomes infected and walled off (typically after week 4) — a step-up approach (drainage before open surgery) is now preferred.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is FALSE. Early surgery in acute pancreatitis dramatically increases mortality. The current standard is aggressive supportive care (fluid resuscitation, enteral nutrition, analgesia); surgical or endoscopic intervention is reserved for infected necrosis that fails conservative management, ideally delayed beyond 4 weeks.
